jobs.title: Customer Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Dana is a global leader in the supply of highly engineered driveline, sealing, and thermal-management technologies that improve the efficiency and performance of vehicles with both conventional and alternative-energy powertrains. Serving two primary markets – passenger vehicle and commercial truck equipment – Dana provides the world's original-equipment manufacturers and the aftermarket with local product and service support through a network of nearly 100 engineering, manufacturing, and distribution facilities.
Job Purpose

Lead Customer Operations strategy and execution, supporting customers throughout the United States and Canada, through call centers located in Maumee, Ohio, and Toluca, Mexico. Responsible for customer experience, operational performance, employee development, escalation management, business process improvement, digital transformation initiatives, and cross-functional collaboration to support Original Equipment and Aftermarket business objectives.

Organization Scope:

Direct Reports: 12

Indirect Reports: 3

Leadership Positions Managed: Supervisor, Team Leads, Technical Support Specialists, and Customer Service Representatives

Geographic Team Scope: United States and Mexico

Customer Support Scope: United States and Canada

Job Duties and Responsibilities

- Lead a multi-country Customer Operations organization supporting customers throughout the United States and Canada.

- Directly manages Supervisors, Team Leads, Technical Support Specialists, and Customer Service Representatives.

- Provide leadership, coaching, mentoring, employee development, and succession planning.

- Conduct annual performance reviews, mid-year reviews, talent assessments, goal setting, and performance improvement activities.

- Approve employee time off requests and oversee workforce planning and staffing requirements.

- Develop and execute Customer Operations strategies aligned with Aftermarket business objectives.

- Serve as the primary escalation point for critical customer issues impacting service, delivery, order fulfillment, product support, and customer satisfaction.

- Lead cross-functional resolution efforts involving Sales, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Distribution, Finance, Quality, IT, and Technical Support teams.

- Own operational performance metrics including phone performance, chat performance, case management, productivity, response times, escalation resolution, and customer satisfaction.

- Drive achievement of customer service goals includes response within 3 hours and case closure within 24 hours.

- Develop, analyze, and present KPI dashboards, performance reporting, and operational insights to leadership.

- Lead customer operations projects supporting continuous improvement, process improvements, system enhancements, organizational changes, and business growth initiatives.

- Represent Customer Operations in enterprise system implementations and enhancements, including requirements gathering, process design, testing, user acceptance testing, training, and change management activities.

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to develop and enhance customer-facing digital platforms and self-service solutions that improve customer experience and operational efficiency.

- Lead workforce transition initiatives, including organizational restructuring, staffing strategy, recruitment support, onboarding, training, knowledge transfer, and operational stabilization activities.

- Prepare and deliver presentations to customers, leadership teams, and cross-functional stakeholders.

- Represent Customer Operations in leadership meetings, business reviews, and strategic planning discussions.

- Partner with Sales and Customer Account teams to support customer retention, growth opportunities, and customer experience initiatives.

- Travel domestically and internationally, including Mexico, to support employee development, operational alignment, process standardization, and business objectives.

- Drive a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and customer focus.

Decision-Making Authority and Organizational Impact

- Makes decisions regarding workforce planning, staffing recommendations, employee development, performance management, and day-to-day operational execution within Customer Operations.

- Provides leadership and direction to Supervisors, Team Leads, Technical Support Specialists, and Customer Service Representatives.

- Exercises independent judgment in prioritizing customer escalations, operational issues, resource allocation, and service recovery efforts.

- Recommend process improvements, organizational changes, staffing adjustments, and operational initiatives to improve efficiency, customer experience, and business performance.

- Influences cross-functional decision-making through collaboration with Sales, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Distribution, Finance, Quality, IT, and Technical Support organizations.

- Represents Customer Operations in leadership discussions and provides recommendations regarding customer trends, service performance, operational risks, and improvement opportunities.

- Responsible for achieving operational performance objectives related to customer responsiveness, case resolution, productivity, service levels, and customer satisfaction.

Education and Qualifications

- Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Leadership, Operations, or related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered.

- 10 + years in customer operations, customer service, customer experience, or aftermarket experience in a manufacturing/distribution environment preferred.

- Experience leading multi-level teams, including supervisors, team leads, technical support, and customer service professionals.

- Experience managing multi-site and/or multi-country teams preferred.

- Support customers across multiple regions or countries, including the United States and Canada.

- ERP systems, CRM platforms, customer portals, digital tools, and Microsoft Office Suite.

- Salesforce or similar customer relationship management platforms preferred.

- Experience leading or participating in system implementations, process improvement initiatives, and organizational change activities.

- Strong understanding of customer service processes, order management, escalation management, case management, and customer support operations.

- Ability to travel domestically and internationally as required.

Skills and Competencies

- Strategic leadership and operational execution

- Customer escalation management and conflict resolution

- Performance management, coaching, and employee development

- KPI development, analysis, dashboarding, and leadership reporting

- Project leadership, continuous improvement, and change management

- Cross-functional collaboration and influence without direct authority

- Executive, customer, and stakeholder presentation skills

- Workforce planning, staffing coordination, and organizational alignment

- Strong written and verbal communication skills

- Manufacturing, distribution, aftermarket, and customer operations knowledge

- Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, customer-focused environment

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class.

jobs.title: Program Management Intern
jobs.description:
Job Purpose

The Program Management Intern will play an active role in supporting the Light Vehicle Driveline team within the GM/Stellantis Customer group. In this dynamic position, you will gain hands-on exposure across the full vehicle lifecycle, working closely with teams that bring innovative automotive solutions to market. You’ll build real-world experience in customer engagement, cross ‑ functional collaboration, and key commercial processes that drive success in the automotive industry.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities:

- The main responsibility of this position will be to assist in the completion of program management projects

- Support cross-functional communication for project-timing charts and schedules

- Participate in extended support of operations, quality, or engineering

- Ensure adequate resources are assigned; elevate deficiencies

- Act as Dana stakeholder contact for customer program inquiries

- Identify program risks and develop contingency plans

- Work with project activities, publish minutes/tasks, follow up on open issues

Education and Qualifications

Education and Experience Requirements:

- Enrolled in degreed program in Marketing, Communications, Advertising, Sales, Engineering or Business Program

- Previous co-op within automotive industry or Dana is a plus

- Passion for program management

Skills

Required Skills, Abilities, and Attributes:

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.

- Strong written, verbal, and presentation communication skills.

- Effective listening and cross-functional communication abilities.

- Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast ‑ paced environment.

- Capable of performing duties with limited supervision

- Willingness to travel if necessary

- Self-directed, motivated, excellent organizational skills

- Excellent interpersonal skills for interaction with all levels

Benefits

- Benefits:

- Paid internship experience.

- Exposure to product development, product launch life-cycle, and executive-level interaction.

- Opportunities for mentorship and professional long term development.

- Insight into supplier OEM dynamics and the automotive value chain.

At the end of the 10-week internship, each intern will present to Dana leadership, summarizing their projects, learnings, and suggestions for improvement.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class.

jobs.title: Area Sales Manager
jobs.description:
Job Purpose

Responsible for driving profitable sales growth within the French Automotive Aftermarket through new business development, expansion of existing customer relationships, and management of strategic accounts, distributors and buying groups.

• Manage the assigned sales territory.

• Develop and implement a long-term sales strategy aligned with company objectives and growth targets.

• Acquire new customers and identify new business opportunities.

• Develop and grow existing key accounts to achieve sales and profitability targets.

• Expand relationships with major buying groups and strategic customers.

• Identify, appoint and develop independent distributors.

• Negotiate commercial agreements in line with company guidelines.

• Monitor market trends, customer requirements and competitor activities.

• Prepare sales forecasts and business reviews.

• Plan and execute trade fairs, exhibitions and industry events, while representing the company at customer meetings and other commercial activities.

• Collaborate closely with Customer Service, Marketing, Product Management and Supply Chain teams.

Education and Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Engineering or a related field preferred.

• Valid driving licence.

• Fluent French, both written and spoken.

• Fluent English, both written and spoken.

• 5+ years of sales experience within the Automotive Independent Aftermarket (IAM).

• Proven track record in business development and account management.

• Experience managing distributors, key accounts and buying groups.

• Strong knowledge of the French automotive aftermarket.

• Demonstrated experience within the French automotive aftermarket, including buying groups, distributors and major distribution networks, is strongly preferred.

Skills

• Strong commercial and business development mindset.

• Proven ability to acquire new customers and grow existing accounts.

• Excellent negotiation and relationship-building skills.

• Results-oriented with a focus on profitable growth.

• Strong communication and presentation skills.

• Self-motivated and able to work independently.

• Excellent planning, organizational and time management abilities.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Adaptability, cultural awareness and teamwork.

• Ability to identify market opportunities and translate them into sales growth.

• Continuous improvement mindset.

Technical Skills

• Proficient in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.

• Experience with CRM and ERP systems (SAP preferred).

jobs.title: Human Resource Manager
jobs.description:
Dana is a global leader in the supply of highly engineered driveline, sealing, and thermal-management technologies that improve the efficiency and performance of vehicles with both conventional and alternative-energy powertrains. Serving two primary markets – passenger vehicle and commercial truck equipment – Dana provides the world's original-equipment manufacturers and the aftermarket with local product and service support through a network of nearly 100 engineering, manufacturing, and distribution facilities.
Job Purpose

The HR Manager will work with the Facility Leadership and the Business Unit HR function to provide the facility with Human Resource services. He/she is responsible for understanding the business needs of the facility and then translating those needs into HR services to ensure the facility benefits from strategic Human Resource services and standardized processes. He/she is responsible for ensuring both the needs of the business and the needs of the people are met while driving Company’s standardized processes into the facility. He/she is also responsible for driving the strategic labor activities and initiatives as it relates to Union Management and Labor Relations.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

• Coordinate staffing activities (including recruiting, selections, and placement) for the location

• Oversee implementation of Company policies and standardized processes within the Company facility

• Ensure development and implementation facility strategies (i.e. training, safety, compliance, labor)

• Deploy strategies and programs as designed by the Company (e.g. compensation planning, talent management processes)

• Provide feedback to the Facility Leadership, Function and Customers to ensure business needs are met

• Lead positive employee relations programs in the facility

• Provide strategic HR solutions to plant manager and staff

• Facilitate issue resolution between employees and managers, as required

• Perform employee and labor relations duties, including grievance procedures, where applicable

• Coordinate staffing activities (including recruiting, selections, and placement) for the location

• Act as a consultant to Business Leaders for Human Resource issues (i.e., career development, staffing, discipline, performance and talent management)

• Analyze HR metrics and create and implement action plans based on those metrics in line with the Function and/or business objectives

• Ensure development and implementation of training strategy

• Work collaboratively with Lean initiatives to ensure success of continuous improvement

• Help coordinate employee involvement and community involvement teams and/or programs

• Ensure that Affirmative Action plans are in place and implemented: Participate in any OFCCP audits (US Only)

• Coordinate facility(s)’s communication efforts (i.e., newsletters, plant meetings, etc)

• Ensure orientation and induction for newly hired employees and contractors is completed
• Perform internal investigations, prepare necessary documentation, and testify at hearings, as required

• Work with Health & Safety professional to ensure implementation of health & safety programs

• Work collaboratively with geographic lead to ensure alignment process to region

• Implement diversity strategy within the facility

Education and Qualifications

• 5+ years of progressive experience as HR generalist in manufacturing facility. Union facility experience required.

• Bachelor’s Degree in Human Resources or related field or equivalent experience

• Certification in Professional Human Resources (i.e. PHR) preferred.

• Strong understanding of HR Law including FMLA, ADA, HIPPA, EEOC, ADEA

• Natural ability to build strong working relationships with organizational leaders

• Ability to communicate effectively with internal and external customer

jobs.title: QMS & Compliance Manager
jobs.description:
Overview:

Provide strategic leadership, governance and continual improvement of the Quality Management System across Dana Birmingham. Ensure sustained compliance with IATF 16949, VDA 6.3, TISAX, customer-specific requirements and corporate standards whilst supporting operational excellence, business growth and customer satisfaction.

Strategic Leadership:

Lead the development and deployment of the site quality systems strategy, quality objectives and governance framework.
Act as the site subject matter expert for quality system compliance, audit assurance and business process effectiveness.

Quality Systems:

Own, maintain and continually improve the Integrated Management System.
Ensure robust process control, document management, risk-based thinking, lessons learned deployment and compliance with all customer, regulatory and corporate requirements.

Audit & Compliance:

Lead internal, customer, corporate and third-party certification audits.
Ensure audit readiness at all times and effective closure of all findings using robust root cause analysis and verification of effectiveness.

Operational Excellence:

Drive continuous improvement through Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 8D, A3 and DMAIC methodologies.
Improve COPQ, FTT, audit performance, customer metrics and process capability.

Customer Focus:

Act as the senior quality systems interface for customers, certification bodies and key stakeholders.
Support customer confidence through effective communication, governance and performance management.

Apply the above skill set listed in the position summary to achieve the following:

Safety First: Always adheres to Dana Life Safety Rules.

Quality Focussed: All day every day adhering to Dana Life Quality Rules.

1. Quality Management System Governance
1.1 Maintain compliance with IATF 16949, VDA 6.3, TISAX and customer-specific requirements.
1.2 Lead management review activities and quality system performance reporting.
1.3 Maintain effective control of procedures, standards, policies and quality records.
1.4 Ensure quality objectives are deployed and monitored throughout the organisation.

2. Audit and Compliance Leadership
2.1 Develop and manage the annual audit programme.
2.2 Lead certification body, customer and corporate audits.
2.3 Verify effective and timely closure of all non-conformances.
2.4 Report compliance status and risks to senior leadership.

3. Continuous Improvement
3.1 Lead site-wide quality and compliance improvement initiatives.
3.2 Facilitate root cause analysis, corrective action and preventive action activities.
3.3 Drive reductions in COPQ, waste, variation and audit findings.

4. Customer & Business Performance
4.1 Monitor PPM, IPM, FTT, COPQ, warranty and customer scorecards.
4.2 Support customer escalations and quality performance reviews.
4.3 Promote customer satisfaction and proactive issue prevention.

5. Risk Management
5.1 Lead quality system and compliance risk assessments.
5.2 Develop mitigation plans and escalation strategies.
5.3 Ensure lessons learned are embedded across the business.

6. Leadership
6.1 Coach and develop employees in quality systems and auditing.
6.2 Promote accountability, engagement and continuous improvement culture

Base requirements:

Including but not exclusive to:
- Degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality Management or related discipline
- IATF 16949 Lead Auditor qualification
- Proven experience managing Quality Management Systems in a high-volume manufacturing environment
- Expert knowledge of IATF 16949, VDA 6.3, TISAX, APQP, PPAP, FMEA, MSA, SPC and Control Plans
- Experience leading customer, certification body and corporate audits
- Strong understanding of Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies
- Excellent stakeholder management, leadership and communication skills
- Advanced Microsoft Office capability, particularly Excel and PowerPoint
- Ability to influence at all organisational levels

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
Job Purpose

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Program Manager to lead and oversee development programs for Light Vehicle Drive Systems within the Ford Business Team, including new product launches, replacements, and major resourcing initiatives. This role requires strong leadership, cross-functional coordination, and a strategic mindset to ensure successful program execution aligned with customer expectations and business objectives.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

- Lead and manage Light Vehicle Drive Systems programs from concept through launch, including footprint and resourcing activities.

- Assemble and guide cross-functional program teams; develop comprehensive program plans and work breakdown structures.

- Ensure all program deliverables meet design, quality, production, financial, and timing requirements.

- Maintain detailed project schedules and timing charts in alignment with customer and internal expectations.

- Facilitate regular team meetings and program status reviews, driving accountability across Engineering, Quality, Operations, and Purchasing.

- Communicate program status effectively across all levels of the organization and with external stakeholders.

- Identify and resolve program issues using root cause analysis and robust change management processes.

- Serve as primary liaison with customers, representing program interests and participating in customer meetings.

- Monitor program scope, budget, and schedule to ensure compliance with customer specifications.

- Coordinate staffing needs with functional departments to support program execution.

- Oversee design, installation, and validation of production equipment and tooling, ensuring compliance with relevant codes and standards.

- Collaborate with Purchasing to establish pricing, warranty, and delivery targets; support supplier negotiations as needed.

- Optimize program cash flow through timely purchase order coordination and budget management.

- Provide extended support to operations, quality, and engineering beyond typical program requirements.

- Schedule and lead Functional Stage Gate reviews and senior management Stage Gate presentations.

Education and Qualifications

Qualifications:

- Minimum 5 years of experience as a Program Manager in a multinational, matrixed organization.

- Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Business, Operations, or a related field.

- Strong knowledge of APQP and program management methodologies.

- Proficient in financial analysis and budget management.

- Multilingual capabilities (French, German, Spanish, Italian) are a plus.

- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office 365 and presentation tools.

- Proven ability to manage complex negotiations and achieve successful outcomes.

- Skilled in cross-functional team leadership and matrix management.

- Comfortable operating at senior management levels.

- Strong organizational, problem-solving, planning, and decision-making skills.

- Self-driven, proactive, and committed to continuous improvement.

- Demonstrates ownership, accountability, and a collaborative team spirit.
